item.title: Teenage Girl Has Been Missing From the Upper West Side for More Than 6 Weeks: Police
item.dc:creator: Gus Saltonstall
item.description:
Amber Bell was last seen leaving her building on August 12, police said.

The post Teenage Girl Has Been Missing From the Upper West Side for More Than 6 Weeks: Police appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
By Gus Saltonstall

A teenage girl has been missing from the Upper West Side for more than six weeks, the New York Police Department announced on Tuesday.

Amber Bell, 17, was last seen leaving her apartment building at 216 West 63rd Street at 4 p.m. on August 12, police said.

She was last seen wearing a white tank top, white sneakers, and gray sweatpants, NYPD added.

Bell is five feet, four inches tall, and around 140 pounds, according to police.

Anyone with information regarding this incident is asked to call the NYPD’s Crime Stoppers Hotline at 1-800-577-TIPS (8477) or for Spanish, 1-888-57-PISTA (74782).

item.title: Big Tree Falls on Central Park West
item.dc:creator: Gus Saltonstall
item.description:
The tree on Central Park West, between West 94th and 95th streets, showed clear signs of instability in the lead up to its fall.

The post Big Tree Falls on Central Park West appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
By Gus Saltonstall

A large tree crashed to the earth on the Upper West Side sometime late Tuesday or early Wednesday.

The tree fell backward on Central Park West, between West 94th and 95th streets, over the barrier to the park. Prior to its fall, the tree had been stationed on the sidewalk of Central Park West.

The force of the tree ripping out of its roots damaged the surrounding cobblestones and pavement.

Multiple people stopped to gawk and photograph the fallen tree on Wednesday morning. One teenager ducked the yellow tape and attempted to jump and touch the top of the stump after a debate over whether it was taller than a basketball hoop.

He didn’t reach it.

Google Maps imagery from August 2026 shows the tree had clearly been leaning backward.

Multiple “tree care” trucks cleaned up the scene Wednesday morning. The teams were cutting up the tree from its top side and loading the wooden carcass into vehicles.

Thanks to Mark Maas for tipping us off about the downed tree.

item.title: Elevators at Major Upper West Side Train Station Reopen
item.dc:creator: Gus Saltonstall
item.description:
The elevators are back up and running at the West 72nd Street 1, 2, and 3 train station.

The post Elevators at Major Upper West Side Train Station Reopen appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
By Gus Saltonstall

The elevators at a major Upper West Side train station reopened this week.

The two elevators at the West 72nd Street and Broadway 1, 2, and 3 train station are back up and running after more than a year of repair work.

The Rag witnessed multiple people ride the elevators Wednesday morning, and a Metropolitan Transportation Authority worker standing nearby confirmed they were back in service.

The 72nd Street elevators had been closed for replacement work since August 2025. The repairs were connected to “better reliability,” adding “modernized equipment,” creating a “smoother ride,” and “upgrading the security systems,” the MTA said at the time.

Initially, the MTA said the elevators would reopen by March of 2026, which was then pushed back to the summer of 2026, with the work actually concluding at the end of September 2026.

A 90-foot construction staging area was erected outside the West 72nd Street station within Verdi Square for the elevator work, which is still up as of Wednesday morning.

With the elevators back up and running, the staging equipment should come down in the near future.

item.title: Openings & Closings: TALEA Beer Co.; Velvet Cowboy; Kine Musubi; Topman Barbershop; Cafe des Artistes; 7th Street Burger
item.dc:creator: Lisa Kava
item.description:
A female-founded brewery and a Hawaiian comfort-food restaurant are among the newest businesses to open on the UWS.

The post Openings & Closings: TALEA Beer Co.; Velvet Cowboy; Kine Musubi; Topman Barbershop; Cafe des Artistes; 7th Street Burger appeared first on West Side Rag.
item.content:encoded:
By Lisa Kava and Julia Ornedo

TALEA  Beer Co., a female-founded brewery, opened on September 25th at 441 Amsterdam Avenue (between West 81st and 82nd streets). TALEA was founded in 2019 by Tara Hankinson and LeAnn Darland with a mission to expand craft beer “beyond the beer bros,” Hankinson wrote to West Side Rag in an email. The duo sold beer door to door, eventually opening a location in Williamsburg, Brooklyn. They have since opened five other locations in NYC. TALEA brews a variety of beer styles including bestseller Al Dente, an Italian-style Pilsner, and specialty sour beers like Pina Colada Splash and Rainbow Cookie. The Upper West Side location features an all-day menu with “heartier dishes for evenings and weekends,” Hankinson wrote. “Our menu will include brunchy and lunch crowd favorites, entrees for evenings and kid friendly food.” Hankinson and Darland are both moms of young children and wanted to create a space that could work for a date night and for a Sunday morning with the kids, she said. St. James Gate, the Irish pub which closed in 2024, was the last tenant in the space. (Thanks to Ben for the tip.)

Velvet Cowboy, a Western bar, opened on September 29th at  509 Amsterdam Avenue (between West 84th and 85th streets). It is in the space previously occupied by Jacob’s Pickles, which moved in October 2025, and is under the same ownership. Velvet Cowboy features a $5 food menu which includes Texas chili, frito pie and a take on a McRib according to The Infatuation. Reservations for the cocktail lounge are available starting October 1st on Resy, which describes Velvet Cowboy as “inspired by the untamed spirit of the American Southwest.”

Kine Musubi, a Hawaiian musubi restaurant, had a soft opening at 128 West 72nd Street on September 24th.  Musubi is a popular snack food in Hawaii, similar to sushi. It is made with  rice topped with Spam or other savory ingredients and topped with seaweed. The restaurant’s co-founder Chi Ian Chan, grew up in Hawaii and moved to NYC in 2022. He previously had a pop up inside of the restaurant Sushi Nonaka which closed in April 2025. Kine Musubi does not yet have set hours, as the staff is still in training, a representative told West Side Rag via social media. A smoke shop was previously in the space. (Thanks to Myra for the tip.)

Topman Barbershop, a barbershop, opened at 2592 Broadway (between West 97th and 98th streets), on August 22nd. This is the third location for the barbershop and the second on the Upper West Side. Topman opened on West 79th Street (at Amsterdam Avenue), in 2024. Services include men’s haircuts, buzzcuts, shaves, and waxing. Mono Cleaners, a dry cleaner, was previously in the space. (Thanks to Elliot and Karen for the tip.)

ICYMI:

Café des Artistes, the iconic long- time Upper West Side restaurant, which closed in 2009, has announced it will reopen, “returning to its original glamour,” at 1 West 67th Street (between Central Park West and Columbus Avenue), in early 2027. In honor of the reopening, they are asking former diners, staff, and neighbors of Café des Artistes to send memories of the space to memories@cafedesartistesnyc.com. Read West Side Rag’s coverage of this news here.

7th Street Burger, a casual burger place, at 424 Amsterdam Avenue (between West 80th and 81st streets), is temporarily closed due to a gas issue. Read West Side Rag’s coverage of this news here.

The Openings & Closings column wouldn’t be possible without our many tipsters: thank you! Anyone can send tips about openings and closings in the neighborhood to info@westsiderag.com.
